extracted.intended_audience: general readers and students of American Civil War history
extracted.subtask_description: Writing or evaluating popular narrative histories of military campaigns (here, Civil War battles and naval operations), emphasizing explanation of strategy, leadership, logistics, and technology for a broad readership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Doctrine of continuous voyage (blockade law)
rubrics_metrics.description: International law accepted the doctrine of continuous voyage, by which contraband could be taken anywhere on the high seas, provided, of course, that the blockader could prove his case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: if far more goods go into a neutral port (e.g., Matamoras) than that port could legitimately use, the presumption is that the excess is contraband; presumption can become proof by further evidence and justify interception on the high seas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blockade requires a double line of operation
rubrics_metrics.description: The blockade therefore required a double line of operation: one, the old line along the Southern coast, the other, the new line out at sea, and preferably just beyond the three-mile limit outside the original port of departure, so as to kill the evil at its source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical implication: combine coastal blockading with an offshore 'high-seas' blockade to intercept blockade-runners and cut contraband at origin; monitor neutral transshipment points like Nassau and Matamoras.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ship maintenance and overhaul for effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: The Alabama had knocked about so much without a proper overhaul that her copper sheathing was in rags, while she was more or less strained in nearly every other part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintenance (e.g., hull sheathing, regular overhauls) materially affects speed, seaworthiness, and combat performance; a ship in poor repair loses tactical options and survivability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Raider design: favor speed over heavy fighting fit
rubrics_metrics.description: The Alabama was designed for speed rather than for fighting, and, with her great spread of canvas, could sometimes work large areas under sail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose-built commerce raiders emphasize speed, endurance, and cruising range over armor and heavy armament; this trade-off shapes their mission profile (captures and escapes rather than ship-to-ship slugging).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exploit material and tactical advantages in engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Kearsarge had superior speed and stronger hull ... with one-third greater horse power, with fourteen more men in her crew, and with two big pivot guns throwing eleven inch shells with great force at short ranges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Successful captains choose ranges, exploit superior horsepower, crew, armament, and hidden defenses (e.g., concealed chain mantlets) to control the tactical situation and deny enemy options (such as escape to neutral waters).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent enemy escape to neutral waters by positioning
rubrics_metrics.description: The Kearsarge thereupon drew off, so that the Alabama could not easily escape to neutral waters if the duel went against her.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When engaging a vessel near neutral ports, position so as to deny the opponent refuge and force a decisive action in international waters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of reserves at the right moment and place
rubrics_metrics.description: This was the first great battle in which all the chief Federals worked so well together and the first in which the commander-in-chief used reserves with such excellent effect, throwing them in at exactly the right moment and at the proper place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective commanders hold and commit reserves judiciously to reinforce or exploit critical sectors; timing and location of reserve deployment can decide battles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seize and hold key terrain without delay
rubrics_metrics.description: Warren ... seizing, on his own initiative, the Little Round Top, without which the left flank could never have been held.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Immediate initiative to occupy decisive ground (hilltops, strongpoints) can be independently decisive; failure to do so risks losing flanks and the whole position.

rubrics_metrics.name: Synchronization and timing of coordinated attacks
rubrics_metrics.description: The idea had been to synchronize three coöperating movements against Meade's whole position ... But though the central force was ready before nine o'clock it never stepped off till three; so great was Longstreet's delay in ordering Pickett's advance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complex plans requiring multiple simultaneous or sequential movements depend critically on synchronized timing; delays in one element can nullify the entire scheme.

rubrics_metrics.name: Artillery preparation must be accurate and appropriately directed
rubrics_metrics.description: They then continued for some time, preparing the way for the charge, but firing too high and doing little execution against the Federal infantry, who were lying down, mostly under cover.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Artillery must be paced and sighted to effective ranges and targets; misdirected bombardment wastes ammunition and fails to suppress defenders—reserving ammunition for counter-fire and close defense may be prudent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cavalry's role: reconnaissance, outpost, and flanking actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Buford's cavalry suddenly resisting him, as they formed the northwest outpost ... The opposing cavalry ... had fought a flanking battle of their own, but without decisive result.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use cavalry as mobile scouts/outposts to detect and delay enemy movements, to hold key approaches until infantry arrives, and to execute screening or flanking operations; cavalry's early actions can shape the battlefield.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concentration of force vs. supply constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Lee in Pennsylvania was in the midst of a very hostile population and facing superior forces which he could only defeat in one of two difficult ways: either by a sudden, bewildering, and unexpected attack ... or by an impregnable defense on ground that also favored a victorious counter-attack and the subsequent crushing pursuit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commanders must weigh supply and local superiority when choosing between risky offensive maneuvers and defensive positions that enable counter-attacks; logistics can force strategic choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Command character and civil-military relations
rubrics_metrics.description: Lincoln's letter ... I believe you to be a brave and skillful soldier ... I also believe you do not mix politics with your profession ... You have confidence in yourself ... You are ambitious ... beware of rashness, but with energy and sleepless vigilance go forward, and give us victories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluating senior commanders includes personal qualities (bravery, skill, confidence, restrained ambition), avoidance of political meddling, caution against rashness, and the need for energy and vigilance; public criticism within the army undermines command.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staff competence and coordination among chiefs
rubrics_metrics.description: Never did so many Federal chiefs show to such great advantage. No less than five commanded in succession between morning and midnight on the first day, each meeting the crisis till the next senior came up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective staff work and smooth succession/coordination among subordinate commanders are essential; high-performing chiefs and competent staff work can offset other disadvantages.
